To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the institutional embedding of IPs in AR4Ds is challenging, but also creates new opportunities.

(1) IPs can be a powerful vehicle to achieve agricultural development impacts, but (2) their implementation and institutional embedding in present AR4Ds are challenging, (3) this is due to the fact that IPs challenge existing AR4D paradigms, (4) this challenge is not necessarily a bad thing, (5) but requires structural change in AR4Ds and (6) investments in learning and capacity development.

IPs are promising tools for AR4D, but their implementation and institutional embedding is a challenge that requires structural changes in AR4D establishments and a transition from technology-oriented towards system-oriented AR4Ds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to institutionalise IPs and AR4D approaches in a systemic manner.
the question of whether IPs can help to achieve a paradigm shift in AR4D, or if they merely reinforce existing technology-oriented approaches.
how to make the transition to systemic AR4D more effective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IPs are promising, but their success depends on how they are designed and institutionalised.
the IP concept is promising, but that it requires a paradigm shift in the institutional embedding of AR4D.
the institutionalisation of IPs is not yet complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IPs have the potential to contribute to systemic innovation and impact.

the institutional embedding and the implementation of IPs are not only a matter of organisational mandates and incentives, but also of the capacity of AR4D establishments to facilitate and manage interactions between stakeholders and to learn from these interactions and from their own performance.

IPs can contribute to paradigm change in AR4D if they are institutionalised as an integral part of the organisation, and if they are embedded within a broader institutional framework that facilitates systemic innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the institutional embedding of IPs is a key determinant of their success, and that it requires a fundamental change in AR4D approaches, mandates and funding.
the institutional embedding of IPs in AR4Ds is a long-term process.
IPs can be an effective vehicle to achieve paradigm change in AR4D, but only if their institutional embedding is carefully considered.
